comparison: Both evaluate the pupil-OFC relationship (C56-C62). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate temporal specificity and control analyses. Peer reviewers also find this relationship SUPPORTED after temporal specificity testing was provided, though they challenge the noradrenaline-specific interpretation (addressed separately in other concordance records).

Both address mOFC multivariate decoding of entropy (C40-C48, C70-C72). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate controls for value and reward history. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether decoding reflects entropy specifically or is confounded by value, noting 'decoding is not significant in the high entropy condition' and suggesting multivariate value effects may remain after univariate regression.

Both evaluate univariate fMRI activations (C30-C36). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate multiple comparisons correction. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting these basic univariate contrasts between explore and exploit phases without challenge.

Both address pupillometry methodology and interpretation (C49-C52, C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting appropriate transparency about limitations in attributing pupil changes specifically to noradrenaline. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, strongly challenging noradrenaline specificity, noting baseline pupil is more related to acetylcholine per Reimer et al. 2016, and recommending reference to 'pupil-linked arousal' instead.

Both address basic pupillometry observations (C53-C55). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate preprocessing. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the descriptive measurements themselves while challenging interpretation of what pupil reflects (addressed in separate concordance record).

Both evaluate behavioral entropy effects (C28). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong statistics (t18=7.60, p=2.57×10⁻⁷). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether model-based entropy affects behavior beyond simple reinforcement learning or win-stay lose-shift effects.

Both address ACC findings (C63, C66, C74, C89, C91, C96). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate correction, noting lack of direct ACC-mOFC relationship as appropriate negative finding. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the double dissociation and ACC-pupil prediction while noting the study cannot dissociate ACC's multiple functions.

Both address the negative finding of no direct ACC-mOFC relationship (C67). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting this may reflect low SNR in brain-brain comparisons. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting this null result as supporting indirect influence via neuromodulatory systems.

Both address theoretical background on entropy and transition functions (C3, C10, C13-C15). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriate theoretical context with relevant citations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns that the mechanistic reasoning conflates computational and implementational levels, noting 'there is nothing, mathematically speaking, that requires a model of inference to inject entropy.'

Both address noradrenaline-specific claims in study framing (C4, C21-C23). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting C4 appropriately frames hypothesis but acknowledging limitations. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, stating authors 'should refrain from linking their results specifically to the LC-NA system' given pupil reflects both noradrenaline and acetylcholine.

Partial overlap on main findings summary (C70-C72). OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretation UNCERTAIN due to inferential leaps about causality and noradrenaline specificity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN specifically about entropy decoding confounds with value. Both identify limitations in causal and mechanistic claims but focus on different aspects.

Both address basic decoding in sensory/motor cortices (C40-C41). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as part of broader multivariate analysis. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting lack of entropy sensitivity in visual and motor cortex without challenge.

Both address hippocampus finding and alternative interpretations (C43, C78). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caution about effect not surviving whole-brain correction. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the appropriately qualified presentation of this marginal finding.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details and participant characteristics (C24-C27, C103-C108) as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and power analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates directional specificity of transitions (C68-C69, exploit→explore but not explore→exploit) as SUPPORTED though interpretation is somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates ACC discussion in relation to prior literature (C86-C95) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and acknowledged limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates detailed methodological specifications (C109-C119) including Bayesian model, fMRI parameters, and preprocessing as SUPPORTED with appropriate and standard procedures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these technical methods claims.

OpenEval evaluates the methodological choice to analyze exploit trials (C37) as SUPPORTED and well-justified for isolating belief updating independent of action changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific methodological decision.
